item.title: Benfotiamine
item.description:
What it is: Benfotiamine is a fat-soluble form of vitamin B1 that crosses cell membranes more effectively than standard thiamine. It supports nerve health, metabolic function, and protects against glycation.

Benefits

Nerve Health & Neuroprotection

  • Supports peripheral nerve function
  • May help with neuropathic pain
  • Supports myelin formation
  • Protects nerves from oxidative stress
  • Anti-inflammatory in nerve tissue

Anti-Glycation Support

  • Prevents advanced glycation end products
  • Reduces protein damage from glucose
  • Supports vascular health
  • Complements blood sugar management

Metabolic Support

  • Essential cofactor for energy metabolism
  • Supports ATP production in mitochondria
  • Enhances carbohydrate metabolism
  • Supports healthy glucose response

Antioxidant Protection

  • Reduces oxidative stress
  • Protects cellular proteins and lipids
  • Supports mitochondrial function

Dosage

Nerve health: 100-150 mg daily Enhanced: 150-200 mg daily Full: 200-300 mg daily Timing: With meals containing fat Duration: 4-8 weeks initial; 12+ weeks for nerve benefits

item.title: Lutein & Zeaxanthin
item.description:
What it is: Lutein and zeaxanthin are carotenoid antioxidants concentrated in the macula (central retina) that protect against light-induced damage and oxidative stress. Research shows supplementation reduces age-related macular degeneration (AMD) risk—the leading cause of vision loss in aging.

Benefits

Eye Health & Vision

  • Accumulates in macula (protective pigment)
  • Reduces glare sensitivity
  • Improves visual comfort and clarity
  • Supports contrast sensitivity
  • Enhances color vision

Macular Degeneration Prevention

  • Reduces AMD (age-related macular degeneration) risk
  • Protects against vision loss with aging
  • Slows AMD progression if present
  • Best evidence for age-related vision protection
  • Particularly valuable for those 50+

Antioxidant Protection

  • Protects retina from oxidative damage
  • Filters harmful blue light
  • Reduces photooxidative stress
  • Supports overall eye health

Cognitive Benefits (Emerging)

  • Lutein crosses blood-brain barrier
  • May support cognitive function
  • Brain antioxidant protection
  • Emerging brain health benefits

Dosage

Vision support: 10-15 mg daily Enhanced AMD prevention: 15-20 mg daily Timing: With meals containing fat (enhances absorption) Duration: 8-12 weeks for initial effects; 12+ weeks for full benefits

item.title: NAC (N-Acetylcysteine)
item.description:
What it is: NAC (N-Acetylcysteine) is a modified form of the amino acid cysteine that serves as the rate-limiting precursor to glutathione—the body’s master antioxidant and primary detoxification molecule. NAC replenishes depleted glutathione stores, supporting respiratory health, immune function, liver detoxification, and cellular protection across multiple organs.

What Is NAC?

NAC is a stable, bioavailable form of cysteine that crosses the blood-brain barrier and reaches intracellular compartments. Once absorbed, NAC is converted to cysteine, which is incorporated into glutathione (GSH)—a tripeptide that serves as the body’s primary endogenous antioxidant and detoxification enzyme. Glutathione cannot be directly supplemented (degraded in GI tract), making NAC the most effective oral precursor.

item.title: Pomegranate Extract
item.description:
What it is: Pomegranate extract from Punica granatum fruit is rich in punicalagins and anthocyanins that support cardiovascular health, reduce inflammation, and provide potent antioxidant protection.

Benefits

Cardiovascular Health

  • Reduces blood pressure (5-8 mmHg typical)
  • Improves endothelial function and blood flow
  • Reduces arterial plaque formation
  • Supports cholesterol profiles
  • Anti-inflammatory in cardiovascular system

Antioxidant Protection

  • Punicalagins among most potent antioxidants known
  • Protects against LDL oxidation
  • Protects cellular DNA
  • Supports mitochondrial health
  • Anti-aging antioxidant support

Anti-Inflammatory

  • Reduces TNF-alpha and IL-6
  • Systemic inflammation reduction
  • Supports joint health

Sexual Function Support

  • Improves blood flow to tissues
  • May improve erectile function
  • Improved nitric oxide and endothelial function

Dosage

Cardiovascular: 250-500 mg daily Enhanced: 500-750 mg daily Full: 750-1,000 mg daily Timing: With meals containing fat Duration: 4-8 weeks cardiovascular; 8+ weeks antioxidant benefits

item.title: Carnosine
item.description:
What it is: Carnosine is a naturally occurring dipeptide (two-amino-acid compound) found abundantly in muscle and brain tissue. It’s a powerful buffer against lactic acid buildup, protects cells from oxidative stress through antioxidant and anti-glycation mechanisms, and shows promising anti-aging effects in research—particularly for muscle preservation and cognitive function during aging.

What Is Carnosine?

Carnosine (beta-alanyl-L-histidine) is a compound synthesized in the body from the amino acids beta-alanine and histidine. It accumulates naturally in skeletal muscle and the brain, where it plays multiple protective roles.

item.title: Chaga Mushroom
item.description:
What it is: Chaga is the most antioxidant-dense natural source ever tested, containing exceptional polyphenol levels for cellular protection and longevity support. Harvested from birch trees in cold climates and used for centuries in Siberian medicine, it fights free radicals and supports immune resilience at the deepest cellular level.

What Is Chaga Mushroom?

Chaga (Inonotus obliquus) is a parasitic fungus that grows on birch trees in cold climates. Despite its unprepossessing appearance (a black, charred-looking growth), Chaga is extraordinarily rich in antioxidants — containing more free-radical-fighting polyphenols than any other natural source tested.

item.title: Maitake Mushroom
item.description:
What it is: Maitake is a medicinal mushroom rich in beta-glucans—complex carbohydrates that directly activate immune cells. Extensively researched in Japan and gaining recognition in Western medicine, maitake supports immune resilience, cardiovascular health, and cellular resilience through multiple mechanisms distinct from typical supplements.

What Is Maitake?

Maitake (Grifola frondosa), known as “dancing mushroom” in Japanese due to its distinctive appearance, is a shelf fungus native to Asia. Unlike culinary mushrooms, maitake has been used medicinally for centuries and is now recognized for its immunomodulating polysaccharides.

item.title: Moringa
item.description:
What it is: Moringa is a nutrient-dense superfood containing complete amino acids, exceptional antioxidants (7x more vitamin C than oranges, 10x more vitamin A than carrots), and minerals in concentrated form. Cultivated for millennia in African and Asian traditions, modern research confirms it as one of the most nutrient-complete plant sources available.

What Is Moringa?

Moringa (Moringa oleifera), also called the “drumstick tree” or “miracle tree,” is a tropical deciduous tree native to India. Often called the most nutrient-dense plant on Earth, moringa leaves have been used in traditional medicine and as food for over 2,000 years.

item.title: Shiitake Mushroom
item.description:
What it is: Shiitake is a culinary and medicinal mushroom rich in lentinan—a beta-glucan polysaccharide with powerful immune-modulating properties. Contains ergothioneine and vitamin D precursors that convert to active vitamin D when exposed to sunlight, making it unique among mushroom supplements for supporting both immune function and vitamin D status.

What Is Shiitake?

Shiitake (Lentinula edodes) is an edible mushroom native to East Asia, now cultivated worldwide. While commonly consumed as food, medicinal-grade extracts concentrate the active immune compounds—particularly lentinan, a well-studied polysaccharide.

item.title: Tart Cherry
item.description:
What it is: Tart cherry is a fruit extract rich in anthocyanins—powerful antioxidants and anti-inflammatory compounds that improve sleep quality, reduce muscle soreness, and support recovery. Clinical research shows it works comparably to some sleep medications without side effects, making it one of the most evidence-backed natural sleep aids available.

What Is Tart Cherry?

Tart cherry (Prunus cerasus) is a sour cherry variety grown primarily in North America, distinct from sweet cherries commonly eaten fresh. While tart cherries are too sour for fresh consumption, they’re ideal for juices, concentrates, and supplements—forms that concentrate their bioactive compounds.

item.title: Elderberry
item.description:
What Is Elderberry?

Elderberry (Sambucus nigra) is a dark purple berry from the European elder tree that has been used medicinally for thousands of years. Ancient Egyptians, Greeks, and Native Americans all recognized its healing properties. Modern science has validated many traditional uses, particularly for immune support and antiviral activity.

Key Active Compounds:

  • Anthocyanins: The deep purple pigments (cyanidin-3-glucoside, cyanidin-3-sambubioside) responsible for potent antioxidant and antiviral effects
  • Flavonoids: Quercetin, rutin, and kaempferol providing anti-inflammatory and immune-modulating activity
  • Phenolic acids: Chlorogenic acid and caffeic acid contributing to antioxidant capacity
  • Lectins: Sambucus nigra agglutinins (SNAs) with immunostimulatory properties
  • Polysaccharides: Complex carbohydrates that activate macrophages and enhance immune surveillance

item.title: Milk Thistle (Silymarin)
item.description:
What Is Milk Thistle?

Milk thistle (Silybum marianum) is a flowering herb native to the Mediterranean region, used medicinally for over 2,000 years. The active compound, silymarin, is extracted from the plant’s seeds and consists of several flavonolignans, with silybin (silibinin) being the most potent and abundant.

Silymarin has earned its reputation as the premier natural liver protector, backed by extensive clinical research demonstrating its ability to protect liver cells from toxins, support regeneration of damaged liver tissue, and enhance the body’s natural detoxification processes.

item.title: How to Boost Glutathione: The Master Antioxidant for Detox & Immunity
item.description:
What Is Glutathione & Why It Matters

Glutathione (γ-L-glutamyl-L-cysteinyl-L-glycine, GSH) is a tripeptide thiol compound present in virtually every cell, functioning as:

The “Master Antioxidant”

  • Neutralizes free radicals (ROS, reactive oxygen species)
  • Regenerates other antioxidants (Vitamin C, E)
  • 1,000+ times more abundant intracellularly than plasma antioxidants
  • Reduces oxidative stress biomarkers by 30-50% when optimized

The “Master Detoxifier”

  • Phase II liver enzyme cofactor: Glutathione-S-transferase (GST)
  • Binds to heavy metals (mercury, lead, cadmium) for excretion
  • Neutralizes xenobiotics (pesticides, industrial chemicals)
  • Prevents 80%+ of endogenous toxin accumulation

The Immune Booster

  • T-cell proliferation regulator: adequate GSH = 3x higher T-cell count
  • IL-2 production amplifier: strengthens Th1 immune response
  • Microbiota support: GSH influences beneficial bacteria colonization
  • Inflammation modulator: reduces TNF-α, IL-6, IL-8 by 20-30%

The Cellular Protector

  • DNA repair cofactor: protects genomic integrity
  • Mitochondrial integrity: maintains ATP production in organelles
  • Nrf2 pathway activator: upregulates 300+ cytoprotective genes
  • Neurological protection: crosses blood-brain barrier; stabilizes dopamine/glutamate

Why Glutathione Levels Decline

Age-Related Decline

  • Peak: 20s-30s (highest intracellular GSH concentration)
  • Decline Rate: 10-15% per decade after age 30
  • By age 65: ~50% reduction in baseline GSH
  • Mechanism: Decreased gamma-glutamylcysteine synthetase (GCL) expression; reduced precursor availability

Lifestyle Depletion

  • Chronic stress: Cortisol increases ROS → consumes GSH (20-30% reduction per week of elevated cortisol)
  • Poor sleep: <7 hours reduces GSH synthesis by 35-40%
  • Sedentary lifestyle: No exercise-induced Nrf2 activation; GSH stagnates
  • High-intensity exercise without recovery: Acute 40-60% GSH depletion; regenerates in 24-48 hours if recovery adequate
  • Poor diet: Low cysteine/glycine/glutamate intake limits GSH synthesis
  • Circadian disruption: Night shift work reduces GSH by 25-35%

Environmental Toxin Exposure

  • Air pollution: Particulate matter & NOx consume GSH (15-25% reduction in urban dwellers)
  • Heavy metals (lead, mercury, cadmium): GSH conjugation depletes stores
  • Pesticides/herbicides: Xenobiotic burden increases GSH turnover 2-3x
  • Mold/mycotoxins: Activate immune response; rapid GSH depletion
  • BPA & plasticizers: Xenoestrogenic compounds increase oxidative stress

Disease States

  • Chronic infections (Lyme, viral): GSH depleted by immune activation
  • HIV/AIDS: Dramatic GSH depletion; strong biomarker for disease progression
  • Lung disease (COPD, asthma): GSH consumed by airway inflammation
  • Liver disease: Reduced synthesis; impaired detoxification
  • Neurodegeneration (Parkinson’s, Alzheimer’s): Brain GSH drops 40-60%
  • Cancer: Tumor cells steal GSH from normal tissue

Medications That Deplete GSH

  • Acetaminophen (Tylenol): Critically depletes GSH in liver
  • Statins: Reduce cellular GSH by 15-20%
  • Antibiotics (especially fluoroquinolones): Inhibit GCL enzyme
  • Immunosuppressants: Reduce lymphocyte GSH
  • Chemotherapy: Severe, temporary depletion

How to Test Glutathione Levels

Gold Standard Testing

Test What It Measures Normal Range Cost Availability
Red Blood Cell (RBC) GSH Intracellular GSH status (most reliable) 160-280 nmol/mL $150-250 Specialty labs (WellnessFX, Cleveland Clinic)
Plasma GSH Circulating (oxidized) form; less relevant 2-5 μmol/L $100-150 Most advanced labs
GSH/GSSG Ratio Oxidative stress indicator; high = healthy >2:1 $200-300 Specialty labs

Most Useful: RBC GSH + GSH/GSSG ratio provides complete picture

item.title: Astaxanthin
item.description:
What Is Astaxanthin?

Astaxanthin is a xanthophyll carotenoid, a lipid-soluble pigment produced by the microalga Haematococcus pluvialis as a stress response mechanism. This compound is responsible for the red coloration in salmon, shrimp, and krill. Unlike other carotenoids, astaxanthin possesses a unique molecular structure featuring ionone rings at both ends with a conjugated polyene chain, allowing it to embed itself across the entire thickness of the cell membrane.

item.title: Green Tea Extract / EGCG
item.description:
What Is Green Tea Extract / EGCG?

Green tea extract is a concentrated form of the bioactive compounds found in green tea (Camellia sinensis), with EGCG (epigallocatechin-3-gallate) being the primary and most potent catechin. While green tea has been consumed for over 4,000 years in Asian cultures, modern extraction technology allows for standardized, high-potency supplements that deliver therapeutic doses impossible to achieve through tea consumption alone.

item.title: Lutein & Zeaxanthin
item.description:
What Is Lutein & Zeaxanthin?

Lutein and zeaxanthin are xanthophyll carotenoids, lipid-soluble pigments that humans cannot synthesize and must obtain through diet or supplementation. These two compounds, along with meso-zeaxanthin (a metabolite of lutein), constitute the macular pigment - a yellow protective layer concentrated in the fovea centralis, the region of highest visual acuity in the retina.

Source and Natural Distribution:

  • Dietary sources: Dark leafy greens (kale, spinach), egg yolks, corn, orange peppers, and marigold flowers
  • Supplement origin: Primarily extracted from marigold flowers (Tagetes erecta) containing 80-90% lutein and 5-10% zeaxanthin
  • Macular concentration: The macula contains 1000x higher concentration than any other tissue, with zeaxanthin predominating in the foveal center and lutein in the peripheral macula

item.title: Manganese
item.description:
What Is Manganese?

Manganese is an essential trace mineral involved in metabolic processes, bone formation, and antioxidant defense. While required in only small amounts (2-5 mg daily), manganese deficiency impairs metabolism, joint health, and oxidative stress management.

Manganese exists in oxidation states from Mn2+ to Mn7+, with Mn2+ and Mn3+ being biologically relevant. The body has limited homeostatic mechanisms for excess manganese, making toxicity possible with supplementation or environmental exposure.

item.title: Quercetin
item.description:
What Is Quercetin?

Quercetin is a polyphenolic flavonoid found abundantly in plant foods, particularly apples, red onions, green tea, berries, and cruciferous vegetables. It exists as a glucose conjugate (quercetin-4’-glucoside) in foods, which is cleaved by gut bacteria into the aglycone form (free quercetin) for absorption.

item.title: Resveratrol
item.description:
What Is Resveratrol?

Resveratrol (3,5,4’-trihydroxystilbene) is a polyphenolic phytoalexin produced by plants as a defense response to fungal infection, UV radiation, and physical stress. It exists in two forms:

  • Trans-resveratrol (biologically active): The naturally occurring form from grapes, red wine, and plant stress responses
  • Cis-resveratrol (biologically inert): An isomer produced by heat or photodegradation; lacks SIRT1 activation capacity

Natural Sources:

  • Red grapes and red wine: 0.5-5 mg/L (varies by vintage and region)
  • Japanese knotweed: 1-2 g per 100g (highest natural concentration)
  • Peanuts, blueberries, mulberries: 0.1-1 mg per 100g

item.title: Alpha-Lipoic Acid
item.description:
What Is Alpha-Lipoic Acid?

Alpha-lipoic acid (ALA), also called lipoic acid, is a small, water- and fat-soluble antioxidant compound synthesized in the mitochondria. Unlike most antioxidants that function in either aqueous or lipid environments, ALA works in both—making it exceptionally versatile at neutralizing reactive oxygen species throughout cellular compartments.

ALA is classified as a universal antioxidant because it can:

  1. Directly neutralize free radicals
  2. Regenerate other antioxidants (vitamin C, vitamin E, glutathione)
  3. Support cellular energy production
  4. Facilitate blood sugar control
  5. Support nerve health

While ALA is synthesized endogenously, production declines with age. Supplementation typically exceeds dietary intake by 100-1000 fold, making supplementation necessary for therapeutic benefit.

item.title: CoQ10
item.description:
What Is CoQ10?

Coenzyme Q10 (CoQ10), also called ubiquinone, is a naturally occurring coenzyme found in every cell in your body. It’s essential for:

  1. ATP Production — the energy currency of cells
  2. Antioxidant Defense — protecting cells from oxidative damage
  3. Cellular Signaling — regulating important biological processes

While your body produces CoQ10, production declines with age (dropping 50% by age 60) and is depleted by certain medications, particularly statins.

CoQ10 is especially critical for high-energy organs: the heart, brain, liver, and kidneys.

item.title: Curcumin
item.description:
What Is Curcumin?

Curcumin is the primary active compound in turmeric (Curcuma longa), a golden spice used for thousands of years in Ayurvedic and Traditional Chinese Medicine. It comprises only 2-8% of turmeric by weight, which is why standardized curcumin extracts are far more potent than turmeric powder alone.

Curcumin is a polyphenol—a class of plant compounds with powerful antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties. It’s one of the most researched natural compounds, with over 12,000 published studies demonstrating benefits across numerous health conditions.

item.title: PQQ (Pyrroloquinoline Quinone)
item.description:
What Is PQQ?

Pyrroloquinoline quinone (PQQ) is a small quinone molecule that functions as a powerful redox cofactor and cellular signaling compound. First discovered in bacteria in 1979, PQQ has emerged as one of the most exciting longevity and cognitive enhancement compounds in biohacking circles.

PQQ is unique among supplements because it:

  1. Stimulates Mitochondrial Biogenesis — the creation of entirely new mitochondria
  2. Functions as a Potent Antioxidant — up to 5,000 redox cycles vs. 4 for vitamin C
  3. Activates Nerve Growth Factor (NGF) — supporting neuroplasticity and brain health
  4. Protects Neurons — from oxidative stress and excitotoxicity

PQQ is considered a novel vitamin-like compound: While not yet classified as an essential vitamin, research suggests PQQ may be conditionally essential for optimal human function.

item.title: Selenium
item.description:
What Is Selenium?

Selenium is an essential trace mineral that serves as a cofactor for selenoproteins — over 25 proteins that are crucial for antioxidant defense, thyroid function, and immune response.

While selenium deficiency is uncommon in developed countries, suboptimal intake affects an estimated 1 billion people worldwide, particularly those in selenium-poor regions (parts of Europe, China, Africa).

Unlike most nutrients, there’s a narrow therapeutic window for selenium — adequate intake is beneficial, but excess is toxic.

item.title: Vitamin E
item.description:
What Is Vitamin E?

Vitamin E is a fat-soluble antioxidant that protects cell membranes from oxidative damage caused by free radicals. Unlike most vitamins, vitamin E actually refers to a family of eight compounds called tocopherols and tocotrienols — alpha, beta, gamma, and delta forms of each.

Your body uses vitamin E throughout the nervous system, muscles, and tissues to prevent oxidative stress. Despite its importance, surveys show approximately 90% of Americans consume less than the recommended daily amount through food alone.

item.title: Spirulina
item.description:
What Is Spirulina?

Spirulina is a blue-green algae (Arthrospira platensis and Arthrospira maxima) that grows in both fresh and saltwater environments. Despite being classified as a “superfood” relatively recently in Western health circles, spirulina has been consumed for centuries — the Aztecs harvested it from Lake Texcoco, and it remains a traditional food source around Lake Chad in Africa.

What makes spirulina remarkable is its extraordinary nutrient density. Gram for gram, it contains more protein than beef, more beta-carotene than carrots, and more iron than spinach. NASA has studied it as a potential food source for astronauts, and the United Nations has recognized it as a tool for combating malnutrition.

item.title: Vitamin C
item.description:
What Is Vitamin C?

Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) is a water-soluble vitamin that humans cannot synthesize — we must get it from food or supplements. It’s one of the most important antioxidants and plays critical roles in immune function, collagen synthesis, and protecting cells from oxidative damage.

Despite being the most commonly supplemented vitamin, true vitamin C deficiency (scurvy) is rare, but suboptimal levels are common. Requirements increase significantly during illness, stress, and exposure to pollutants.

item.title: Zinc
item.description:
What it is: Zinc is an essential mineral required for immune function, testosterone production, and enzyme activity across 300+ metabolic pathways. With an estimated 2 billion people deficient, zinc supplementation supports rapid immune response, sexual health, wound healing, and skin integrity across all ages.

What Is Zinc?

Zinc is an essential trace mineral involved in over 300 enzymatic reactions and critical for immune function, protein synthesis, wound healing, DNA synthesis, and cell division. It’s the second most abundant trace mineral in the body after iron.
